- Valid output is exactly an `(11, 2)` array-like collection, converted to `numpy.ndarray`, with every point satisfying the triangle half-plane tests within `TOL = 1e-6`. Any exception, wrong shape, or outside point yields `combined_score = 0.0`. The evaluator checks all \(\binom{11}{3}=165\) point triples.
- `min_area_normalized` is the geometric objective:  
  \[
  \min_{i<j<k}\operatorname{area}(p_i,p_j,p_k)\ /\ (\sqrt{3}/4).
  \]
  Larger is better. It is reported directly but has no separate aggregation weight in evaluator code.
- `combined_score` is the effective benchmark score:  
  \[
  \text{combined\_score}=\text{min\_area\_normalized}/0.036529889880030156
  \approx 27.3748\cdot\text{min\_area\_normalized}.
  \]
  Thus its only scored component has weight 1 on normalized minimum area, equivalently weight about `27.3748` on raw normalized area. A score of `1.0` corresponds to normalized minimum area `0.036529889880030156` (raw Euclidean triangle area about `0.015817`).
- `eval_time` is returned but is not included in `combined_score`, has no stated cutoff or penalty, and therefore is not an evaluator-visible quality tradeoff unless an external system separately ranks it. Do not sacrifice minimum area for faster optimization; once a good configuration is found, returning a stored configuration makes call time negligible anyway.
- There are no opposing weighted terms: `min_area_normalized` and `combined_score` are exactly monotone versions of the same quantity. The largest and only quality lever is raising the worst of the 165 triangle areas. The benchmark `1.0` is a reference threshold, not a demonstrated maximum; without an incumbent result, no term can truthfully be classified as numerically near its maximum.
- The nominal Heilbronn goal and the evaluator goal coincide. Nothing rewards visual regularity, average triangle area, pairwise separation, symmetry, optimizer convergence diagnostics, or robustness beyond valid output; these are useful only insofar as they improve the minimum triple area.
- The submitted function receives no instance input at all: this is a fixed, complete, offline/batch optimization problem. Perform expensive global search before submission, then return a deterministic cached point set. There is no need for an online, causal, or streaming algorithm.

EXAMPLES OF DIFFERENT approaches:
- Offline cached-construction approach; use `scipy.optimize.differential_evolution` offline to optimize all 22 coordinates against the minimum over all 165 absolute determinant areas, then submit the best fixed feasible arrangement. This directly improves the sole scored quantity while avoiding evaluation-time search.
- Stochastic global continuous search; `scipy.optimize.differential_evolution` and `scipy.optimize.dual_annealing` with fixed seeds, multiple independent restarts, and a triangle-coordinate parameterization. Parameterize points by nonnegative barycentric coordinates so every candidate remains inside the triangle rather than relying on post-hoc clipping that can reduce the bottleneck area.
- Deterministic global-search cross-check; `scipy.optimize.shgo` on reduced-coordinate or structured subproblems. Its evaluator-visible role is to find or certify alternative basins missed by stochastic methods, not to improve unscored aesthetics.

- Store the best offline-discovered coordinates as deterministic constants; verify all 165 areas using the evaluator’s absolute-determinant formula and retain only candidates with a strict interior feasibility margin larger than numerical noise.
- Use barycentric-coordinate bounds or inequality constraints with an inward margin such as `1e-8` to `1e-7`; this preserves the `1e-6` containment requirement without depending on tolerance exploitation.
- For `scipy.optimize.differential_evolution`, increase `popsize`, `maxiter`, restart count, and final `polish=True`; use fixed integer `seed` values and keep the best exact minimum-area result across seeds.

Gain mechanism: Canonicalize each terminal configuration under the six rigid symmetries of the outer equilateral triangle by choosing the lexicographically smallest sorted barycentric representation. Replace that cluster with the corresponding four points from the second parent selected by nearest barycentric location to those cluster positions; keep the remaining seven points from the first parent. Every copied point remains valid because it is already inside the triangle. Rank all hybrids using the exact 165-triple objective and signed-polish only the six best hybrids, assigning signs separately for every hybrid. This permits a coordinated four-point relocation across a barrier that single-point annealing moves and fixed-sign polishing cannot traverse, while retaining the seven-point scaffold responsible for the source configuration’s existing bottlenecks.

Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless a hybrid after exact scoring and polishing exceeds `min_area_normalized = 0.0341081063388`; the new falsifiable degree of freedom is a simultaneous four-point barycentric cluster substitution unavailable to the incumbent’s one-point proposals.

strategies.title: [critical-hypergraph-block-repair] Coherent replacement of a bottleneck-connecte
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: critical-hypergraph-block-repair

Replacement scope: Replace the 24 independent full annealing restarts with 12 shorter annealing starts of 25,000 moves, followed by deterministic block-repair searches on the best four endpoints; leave the final signed polishing phase in place.

Compute budget: 12 global starts × 25,000 single-point moves; then, for each of the best 4 endpoints, at most 3 block repairs. Each repair uses one 4-point block differential-evolution search with population 10 and at most 180 generations, followed by at most 250 SLSQP iterations on that block only. The six frozen-anchor points are not optimizer variables. This is bounded near the existing annealing cost and should not materially exceed the current runtime.

Gain mechanism: Build a weighted 3-uniform critical hypergraph from the endpoint’s 30 smallest absolute determinants, assigning each point a weight equal to the sum of inverse determinant magnitudes of incident triples. Select the four highest-weight points, except that if this produces fewer than four distinct heavily connected points, complete the block using the strongest hypergraph-neighbor points. Freeze the other seven points. Parameterize each replacement point by folded barycentric coordinates, so every candidate remains in the equilateral triangle. Optimize the four replacement points jointly against the exact minimum determinant over all 165 triples, using a smooth soft-min during differential evolution and exact minimum for acceptance. Then perform a block-only signed SLSQP solve with an auxiliary `t` and signs inherited from the repaired seed. This is a coherent four-point relocation: it can break a locally jammed cluster while preserving the useful global scaffold, unlike the incumbent’s one-point annealing proposals and all-coordinate local polish.

Expected-gain check: exact gain cannot be predicted without evaluating the selected hypergraph blocks, but the incumbent has no move that jointly replaces a connected four-point bottleneck subsystem while holding its successful anchors fixed, and the falsifiable acceptance threshold is evaluator `min_area_normalized > 0.0341081063392`.

strategies.title: [reflection-orbit-launch] Reflection-symmetric low-dimensional basin search foll
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: reflection-orbit-launch

Replacement scope: Replace 8 of the 24 random annealing starts with 4 reflection-orbit structural launches, while retaining the remaining 16 unrestricted annealing starts and retaining the existing endpoint polishing stage.

Compute budget: 4 deterministic structural launches. Each launch uses differential evolution with population 12 and at most 500 generations over 11 scalar variables, then one unrestricted signed SLSQP release of at most 900 iterations. The existing unrestricted annealing budget is reduced from 24 to 16 starts, so this is a replacement of search budget rather than a second unconstrained full pipeline.

Gain mechanism: Search the explicitly reflection-symmetric eleven-point family consisting of five mirrored pairs and one axial point. For each pair generator, use two folded coordinates in the left half-triangle with vertices \((0,0),(0.5,0),(0.5,h)\), expand it by reflection \((x,y)\mapsto(1-x,y)\), and represent the axial point as \((0.5,hq)\), \(q\in[0,1]\). This guarantees all 11 expanded points are feasible. Differential evolution searches the reduced family using exact all-triple minimum determinant evaluation, with deterministic seeds 31001 through 31004. Expand the best symmetric point set and release all 22 coordinates into the existing unrestricted signed maximin SLSQP formulation. The structural launch supplies coordinated mirrored boundary/interior contacts that random individual point proposals are very unlikely to preserve long enough to enter the corresponding basin; the unrestricted release prevents symmetry from imposing a final ceiling.

Expected-gain check: exact gain cannot be predicted before the deterministic orbit searches are run, but the incumbent contains neither equality-tied reflection orbits nor coordinated orbit moves, and the falsifiable evaluator threshold is `min_area_normalized > 0.0341081063392` (combined score \(>0.933704055807\)).

strategies.title: ordered attempt [active-set-homotopy] Soft-min continuation before exact signed maximin polishin
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: active-set-homotopy

Replacement scope: Replace the entire current optional SciPy polishing block beginning at `try: from scipy.optimize import minimize` through its final `except Exception: pass`; retain the annealing phase and its endpoint collection unchanged.

Compute budget: At most 3 selected annealing endpoints; for each endpoint run 3 smooth continuation solves of at most 350 SLSQP iterations each, followed by one exact auxiliary-variable signed-maximin solve of at most 900 iterations. This replaces, rather than adds to, the current two-candidate SLSQP loop, so expected evaluation time is comparable to the current polishing phase.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent immediately optimizes the nonsmooth lower envelope through a fixed signed constraint system, so inactive near-critical triples receive no optimization weight until they abruptly become active. Introduce a continuation objective
\[
-\tau\log\sum_r \exp[-g_r(p)/\tau],
\]
where \(g_r\) includes the signed determinants and the four edge slacks for every point, with positive sign cell inherited from the endpoint. Use \(\tau=(3\cdot10^{-3},10^{-3},3\cdot10^{-4})\), rescaled by the seed minimum determinant if necessary. Each continuation stage starts from the previous stage and has the triangle half-plane inequalities explicitly enforced. Its final point initializes the existing exact `t`-variable SLSQP formulation. This moves points according to the whole near-active determinant spectrum rather than only the current minimum constraints, allowing coordinated resolution of bottlenecks that the direct maximin formulation can leave marginally inactive. Preserve the best annealing result unless the exact all-165-triple determinant check improves it; retain strict `inside` validation before returning.

Expected-gain check: exact gain cannot be predicted without solving, but this introduces soft-min weights for near-active triples that the incumbent’s direct auxiliary-variable objective does not represent, and the falsifiable promotion threshold is evaluator `min_area_normalized > 0.0341081063392`, equivalently combined score \(>0.933704055807\).

strategies.title: [arrangement-best-response] Exact one-point line-arrangement refinement
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: arrangement-best-response  
Replacement scope: Replace the final SLSQP polishing loop after endpoint selection with cyclic exact one-point best-response sweeps, followed by one retained signed maximin polish only for the improved endpoint.  
Compute budget: At most 3 endpoint seeds, 8 full coordinate sweeps per seed, and at most 220 candidate locations per point per sweep; one final SLSQP call per improved seed with at most 700 iterations. Expected evaluation-time effect: modestly lower than the existing two-SLSQP-candidate-per-endpoint phase.  
Gain mechanism: With the other ten points fixed, every determinant involving the moved point is an affine function of its two coordinates. For a trial threshold \(t\), the feasible region is the triangle minus strips around the 45 lines \(|a x+b y+c|<t\). The best value for that point occurs at a triangle-edge/strip-boundary intersection or at an intersection of two determinant-boundary lines. Enumerating these locations gives an exact finite best-response mechanism that can cross orientation cells; the incumbent’s SLSQP polishing stays inside one initially chosen determinant-sign cell. Use the current global best as the initial arrangement, test every candidate after barycentric projection with the exact all-165-triple objective, and accept only strict improvements. All generated candidates are retained only when their barycentric coordinates are nonnegative, so containment is exact. Expected-gain check: this is falsified unless the exact evaluator reports `min_area_normalized > 0.0341081063392`; its new degree of freedom is a single-point move across a determinant-zero strip, which the incumbent’s fixed-sign constraints cannot realize.

strategies.title: [large-neighborhood-reinsertion] Two-point ruin-and-reinsert basin escape
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: large-neighborhood-reinsertion  
Replacement scope: Replace the 24 independent annealing starts with a shorter 12-start annealing stage plus deterministic two-point removal/reinsertion neighborhoods launched from the best four terminal arrangements; retain the existing final validity check and incumbent fallback.  
Compute budget: 12 annealing starts of 40,000 proposals, then at most 10 selected point-pairs per retained endpoint; each pair gets one differential-evolution solve in four barycentric coordinates with population 24 and at most 160 generations, followed only if improved by one 500-iteration SLSQP polish. Expected evaluation-time effect: comparable to or moderately above the current search, but bounded and concentrated on promising terminal basins.  
Gain mechanism: Rank points by their participation count among the 30 smallest absolute determinants, choose pairs that jointly cover many bottleneck triples, freeze the remaining nine points, and reinsert the pair simultaneously. Parameterize each reinserted point by two clipped barycentric weights, with the third weight equal to one minus their sum; use the exact minimum over all 165 determinants as the differential-evolution objective. Unlike one-point annealing moves and local signed-cell polishing, simultaneous removal breaks the coupled bottleneck cluster: triangles containing either removed point can be rebuilt together rather than forcing one member to move while the other remains obstructive. Reject any pair whose fixed-nine-point triples already fall below the current threshold; this is a cheap exact pruning rule. Barycentric coordinates guarantee all replacements remain in the triangle. Expected-gain check: the proposal is falsified unless at least one reinsertion produces `min_area_normalized > 0.0341081063392`; the specific missing freedom is coordinated relocation of both endpoints of a bottleneck-connected pair, unavailable to the incumbent’s single-coordinate annealing proposals.

strategies.title: [absolute-threshold-feasibility] Sign-free threshold continuation with COBYLA
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: absolute-threshold-feasibility  
Replacement scope: Replace the fixed-sign SLSQP endpoint-polishing block entirely with threshold-feasibility continuation on unrestricted barycentric coordinates; preserve the annealing phase solely as a source of feasible lower bounds and seeds.  
Compute budget: At most 4 retained seeds, 12 threshold levels per seed, and 2 COBYLA launches per level with at most 2,000 evaluations each; after the highest feasible threshold, at most one 800-iteration SLSQP polish from the returned feasible arrangement. Expected evaluation-time effect: potentially somewhat higher than the present polishing phase but substantially less than adding another full global annealing pipeline.  
Gain mechanism: For each threshold \(t\), impose the triangle half-plane inequalities and the sign-free constraints \(|\det(p_i,p_j,p_k)|\ge t\) directly. Start from the seed’s exact raw determinant minimum, raise the target by a deterministic bracketed continuation, and use two complementary starts: the prior feasible solution and a barycentric perturbation of it. COBYLA handles the nonsmooth absolute constraints without committing to the seed’s orientation signs, so a feasible path can enter a different oriented-matroid chamber while maintaining the tested threshold. Bisection is performed only after a successful higher threshold has been found, and every returned candidate is independently checked against the exact determinant objective and triangle half-planes. Expected-gain check: this structural route is falsified unless its best exact output exceeds `min_area_normalized = 0.0341081063392`; it explicitly adds feasible orientation-cell changes under a maintained area threshold, which the incumbent’s signed inequalities prohibit.

strategies.title: [bundle-trust-region] Collective nonsmooth active-triple bundle refinement
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: bundle-trust-region

Replacement scope: Replace only the current post-annealing SLSQP polishing block, beginning at `ranked = sorted(endpoints, ...)` and ending immediately before the outer `except Exception`.

Compute budget: At most 3 endpoint seeds; for each seed, at most 80 bundle iterations and 6 trial radii per iteration. Expected evaluation-time effect: modestly lower than the current six SLSQP solves because each iteration uses vectorized determinant and gradient evaluations without finite-difference constraint Jacobians.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent fixes every triple orientation before polishing, so its local optimizer is confined to one signed determinant cell and treats all 165 constraints equally even when only a small set is bottlenecking. Replace that with a deterministic nonsmooth bundle method: at each iterate, select all triples with absolute determinant at most `1.08 * current_minimum`, compute their signed determinant gradients with respect to all 22 coordinates, and solve a trust-region linear program maximizing an auxiliary improvement variable subject to each selected signed linearization increasing by that amount, triangle half-plane margins, and `||delta||_inf <= radius`. Evaluate all 165 exact determinants after every proposed collective step, accept only exact improvements, and shrink or enlarge the radius according to actual-versus-predicted improvement. Every point remains valid by including the four triangle half-plane inequalities directly in the LP and projecting any numerical residue into barycentric coordinates with a `2e-8` inward margin. The bundle is periodically rebuilt from the full triplet set, so newly created bottlenecks are immediately protected rather than being missed by a stale active set.

Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable by requiring the returned exact evaluator metric to exceed normalized minimum area `0.0341081063392`; the incumbent’s fixed-sign SLSQP block cannot make the collective active-set trust-region step that simultaneously balances all currently near-tight triples.

strategies.title: [multiplier-community-relaxation] Dual-weighted mesoscopic point-community reloc
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: multiplier-community-relaxation

Replacement scope: Replace the 24 independent annealing restarts and their endpoint collection with a two-stage process consisting of 12 shorter annealing starts followed by deterministic community relocation from the best four endpoints; retain the existing final signed SLSQP polishing block unchanged.

Compute budget: 12 annealing starts of 30,000 proposals each; from each of the best 4 endpoints, at most 5 community relocations; each relocation has at most 250 SLSQP iterations. Expected evaluation-time effect: approximately comparable to, or below, the present 24-by-40,000 proposal global phase.

Gain mechanism: Construct the hypergraph whose weighted hyperedges are the lowest 24 absolute-determinant triples, weighting each edge by `exp(-(abs(det)-m)/(0.12*m))`, where `m` is the endpoint minimum determinant. Compute point scores from weighted incidence and choose the highest-weight connected component after deleting one articulation point if necessary; this produces a 3-to-6 point mesoscopic community rather than the incumbent’s one-point random moves. Freeze all other points and jointly relocate the selected community in barycentric coordinates, maximizing an auxiliary `t` against every triple involving at least one moved point while preserving the endpoint’s signs for constraints initially above `0.8*m`. Run three deterministic candidate communities per endpoint: the top component, its complement if it has at most six points, and the component obtained after removing the most incident point. This moves a geometrically coupled bottleneck cluster together while the frozen exterior acts as a set of exact exclusion constraints. Use barycentric variables with nonnegative lower bounds `2e-8`, so containment is automatic.

Expected-gain check: accept this construction as successful only if exact re-evaluation gives normalized minimum area above `0.0341081063392`; unlike the incumbent’s single-point annealing proposals, this explicitly unlocks a coordinated 3-to-6-point displacement determined by the active-triple incidence structure.

strategies.title: [order-type-cell-walk] Deterministic oriented-order-type mutation search
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: order-type-cell-walk

Replacement scope: Replace the unrestricted random initialization plus annealing phase, while retaining the existing endpoint ranking and signed SLSQP polishing phase.

Compute budget: At most 18 order-type seeds, each with at most 40 cell mutations; each mutation receives at most 180 SLSQP iterations. Expected evaluation-time effect: lower than the current 960,000 stochastic proposals, although individual constrained solves are more expensive.

Gain mechanism: Search arrangement cells rather than coordinate perturbations. Start from six deterministic interior triangular-lattice jitter seeds and six random barycentric seeds. For each seed, form the sign vector of all 165 determinants and identify the 12 smallest absolute determinants. A cell mutation chooses one such triple and deliberately crosses its determinant-zero wall: move its third point by a signed normal displacement of magnitude `1.5*m / ||b-a||`, where `m` is the current minimum determinant, then restore triangle validity through barycentric projection. This changes exactly the local oriented-matroid relation that the incumbent signed polishing permanently freezes. After each proposed wall crossing, maximize the signed minimum determinant inside the new sign cell using SLSQP with the auxiliary `t`; retain the exact best valid result and branch only from the best two unexplored mutated cells at each depth. Also include mutations that exchange the radial order of two points around the point with highest active-triple incidence, implemented by crossing their collinearity wall with that pivot. All seeds and mutation choices are deterministic, and every trial is maintained inside the triangle through nonnegative barycentric coordinates.

Expected-gain check: this structural route is falsifiable by an exact normalized minimum-area result above `0.0341081063392`; the current optimizer cannot cross a determinant-sign wall during its fixed-sign polishing, whereas this search explicitly explores adjacent order-type cells before polishing them.

strategies.title: [active-manifold-linearization] Nullspace equalization on the signed bottleneck
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: active-manifold-linearization

Replacement scope: Replace the current SLSQP polishing loop beginning at `for endpoint_value, seed in selected:`; retain the annealing phase and its endpoint selection unchanged.

Compute budget: At most 3 endpoint starts, 70 sequential linearized maximin steps per start, and one final SLSQP call of at most 500 iterations per start; expected evaluation time is lower than the current two-SLSQP-candidates-per-endpoint polish, because each linear subproblem has only 23 variables and a restricted active constraint set.

Gain mechanism: The present polish gives all 165 signed determinant inequalities to a generic nonlinear solver at once, so its finite-difference steps are dominated by inactive constraints and it commonly terminates with several nearly active triangles having unequal slack. Instead, at each iterate form the exact determinant Jacobian for the currently active band `abs(det) <= 1.08 * current_min`, retain signed orientations, and solve a bounded linear program in coordinate increments and a scalar improvement `delta`: maximize `delta` subject to first-order signed-area increases for the active triangles, first-order preservation of all triangles within `1.30 * current_min`, triangle-edge linear constraints, and an infinity-norm trust radius. Use `scipy.optimize.linprog(method="highs")`, backtrack the step against the exact 165-triple objective, and enlarge the active band whenever a previously inactive triple becomes limiting. Finish only the best accepted iterate with the existing signed SLSQP formulation and exact determinant Jacobians.

The LP step preserves hard validity by including all three barycentric half-plane inequalities, using a strict inward edge margin such as `2e-8`, and accepting a step only after direct containment and exact-area checks; an unsuccessful LP step leaves the prior feasible point unchanged. strategies.title: [delaunay-flip-neighborhood] Delaunay quadrilateral patch relocation
